
=================================================================
#43 Muryuk  (562)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
Arc: The Chunchu Era · place: daegaya · tone: elegiac legend
Logline: The youngest son in the cart surrenders Gaya on one condition, then spends his life riding for Silla. Even south.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ His name was Muryuk. He was the youngest of three sons in a cart, and the only one who looked back.
[1] [MAP 562: Five hundred years of iron, gone in thirty.]
[2] ¶ For five hundred years the people of Gaya lived by iron and by six eggs, and they enjoyed great peace. Then Silla came shopping.
[3] ── SCENE: The Surrender ──
[4] ¶ The lord of Geumgwan did the arithmetic first. Baekje to the west, Silla to the north, a river of iron and no army worth the name.
[5] ¶ The cart is slow. The road to Surabol is long enough for a boy to change his mind several times.
[6] The lord of Geumgwan: Face front, Muryuk. / Your brothers are facing front.
[7] Kim Muryuk: Somebody should remember what it looked like. / …The harbour. Before.
[8] The lord of Geumgwan: Then remember it quietly. Kings don’t like being reminded what they bought.
[9] ¶ He keeps looking back until the river bends out of sight.
[10] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 4, Silla Annals — King Beopheung, yr. 19 (532); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 86): The lord of Geumgwan, Kim Guhae, came with his queen and three sons, bringing the treasury and precious things of the country, and surrendered.❞
[11] [CARD Kim Muryuk: The youngest son in the cart. Gaya handed over its crown. It did not hand over him.]
[12] ¶ The king on the dais has bought harbours before. He has never bought one that talks back.
[13] Kim Muryuk: If we are to surrender, I have one condition… / Let my father’s sons live in Silla without shame…
[14] King Beopheung: And what do you mean by that?
[15] Kim Muryuk: In Silla… I know a man’s blood decides everything… / Sacred Bone, True Bone… I know it all… / If my descendants — the sons and daughters of Suro and Heo — can take a worthy place… / then I too am ready to give Silla my life…
[16] King Beopheung: Very well. Your descendants shall be raised as True Bones of Silla.
[17] King Beopheung: In return you ride for me. North, west. Wherever the border itches. / …Even south.
[18] Kim Muryuk: …Even south.
[19] ¶ Three generations later, his grandson will still be told he is not really one of them.
[20] Kim Muryuk: Your grace is boundless… Your Majesty…!
[21] ── SCENE: The Night Road ──
[22] ¶ Twenty-two years later he is a Silla governor in a Gaya helm, because nobody has managed to make him take it off. One night on the Gwansan road, the King of Baekje rides into his ditch.
[23] ¶ You have seen that night from the king’s side. From the cone’s side it is shorter. A man who once begged at a king’s feet sits another king on a camp stool and does not draw his sword. The slave does the rest.
[24] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biography of Kim Yushin, part 1): His grandfather Muryeok was Commander of the Army of the Sinju Circuit; he once led troops that captured the king of Baekje and four of his generals and took more than ten thousand heads. His father Seohyun rose to the rank of Sopan, Governor-General of Daeyang Province and Pacifier of all the armies of Daeyang Province.❞
[25] ¶ Ten thousand heads, says the record, and makes him a hero. He goes home and does not eat for two days.
[26] ¶ Before that, the slave who did the cutting comes to his tent with the king’s knife, because nobody else will take it.
[27] Dodo: My lord. They said give it to the Gaya one. / …That’s you, isn’t it?
[28] Kim Muryuk: Keep it. / A knife that’s done that once shouldn’t go home to a man with sons.
[29] ── SCENE: The Last Gate ──
[30] ¶ Eight years after that, the Cloud King comes for what is left of Gaya. He brings a boy-general, Sadaham. He brings Muryuk.
[31] Sadaham: They said too young. / The gate didn’t.
[32] Mugwan: Don’t die first.
[33] Sadaham: Then keep up.
[34] ¶ The tall Gaya cone still fights. The men on Daegaya’s gate wear the same helm Muryuk does.
[35] Kim Muryuk: Those are my father’s helms. / Let me walk up first. Alone.
[36] Sadaham: They’ll shoot you.
[37] Kim Muryuk: Then keep the gate warm for me.
[38] ¶ He walks to the gate with his helm in his hand. Nobody on the wall knows what to do with a Gaya face under a Silla banner. By the time they decide, he is talking. Gaya has always listened to a good price.
[39] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 4, Silla Annals — King Jinheung, yr. 23 (562), 9th month; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 98): In the ninth month Gaya rebelled. The king ordered Isabu to punish them, with Sadaham as deputy. Isabu brought up the army, and they all surrendered at once.❞
[40] ¶ The boy took his prize anyway. After the city fell he opened the prize-cages and kept only Alcheon dirt. Take the land. Leave the people.
[41] Sadaham: Alcheon dirt. / That’s enough.
[42] ¶ Muryuk watches the cages open and says nothing. It is the first Silla habit he has ever liked.
[43] ── SCENE: The Name ──
[44] ¶ He grows old in Surabol with a True Bone seal and a Gaya accent he never loses. His son Seohyun is clever and polite, and keeps walking into things while looking at clouds.
[45] Kim Muryuk: Seohyun. When you have a son— / Don’t give him a Silla name to make them like him. They won’t. / Give him one that keeps faith.
[46] Kim Seohyun: Father, I’m not even— there isn’t even a girl, I—
[47] Kim Muryuk: There will be. You walk into walls looking at clouds. / Some girl will find that charming. One.
[48] ¶ Then he says a name nobody has been given yet.
[49] Kim Muryuk: Yushin…
[50] ══ DAY: DAY 6 ══
[51] ¶ On the sixth night there are two cups on the pavilion table. Bidam poured them himself. Last night he found out whose grandson he has been calling a Gaya ox.
[52] ¶ **Five days of grain. Two cups poured. Will the grandson of the cone helm come to tea…?**
